subjects.title: Childhood and Growing up

units.title: Growth and Development of the Learner Credit- 1
units.topics: 1.1 Heredity and Environment : Meaning and importance of heredity and environment in shaping a child, Concept of social heredity , Educational importance in teaching and learning. 1.2 Growth and Development : Meaning and principles of growth and development, Difference between growth and development, Relation between development and learning. 1.3 Stages of Growth and Development : Stages from infancy to adolescence, Features of adolescence - (physical, mental, emotional, moral, and social aspects) 1.4 Holistic Development and Role of School : Concept and Importance of Holistic development of the learner, Role of school, teacher, and parents in helping adolescents grow holistically. 1.5 Brain Development and Learning : Brain development, Brain development during adolescence, Concept of neuroplasticity and how the brain learns new skills, Implications for classroom learning and teaching. 1.6 Gender Identity and Education : Meaning and development of gender identity among children and adolescents, Difference between sex and gender, Role of teachers in ensuring gender equality and creating an inclusive classroom environment.

units.title: Education and Individual Differences Credit- 1
units.topics: 2.1 Nature and Scope of Individual Differences : Meaning and importance of individual differences, Influence of heredity, environment, culture, and education on learners. 2.2 Causes of Individual Differences : Causes of differences among learners: age, sex, intelligence, multiple intelligences, emotional intelligence, socio -economic background, and interests, Impact of these causes on learning and classroom performance. 2.3 Types of Individual Differences : Personality and behavioral variations such as: Introvert–Extrovert, Active–Passive, Thinker–Feeler, 2.4 Dimensions of Individual Differences : Physical: health, height, strength, and appearance; Cognitive: intelligence, memory, and learning ability ; Social: relationships, cooperation, and communication skills 2.5 Implications for Learning to facilitate holistic development : Understanding learners’ differences to improve teaching for holistic development of learner. 2.6 Managing Learner Diversity : Differentiated teaching strategies for diverse learners, Creating a positive, inclusive, and bias-free classroom environment.

units.title: Learner Diversity in the Classroom Credit- 1
units.topics: 3.1 Learning Styles: Meaning and importance of learning styles, Types of learn ing styles: Visual, Auditory, and Kinesthetic, Teaching strategies to address all learning styles in the classroom. 3.2 Multiple Intelligences Theory (Howard Gardner) : Different kinds of intelligence: linguistic, logical-mathematical, musical, bodily-kinesthetic, interpersonal, intrapersonal, and naturalistic, Application of this theory in teaching- learning. 3.3 Psycho-Social Development (Erik Erikson) : Stages of personality and social development, Identity and role confusion during adolescence, Teacher’s role in supporting emotional and social development. 3.4 Moral Development (Lawrence Kohlberg) : Stages of moral development; Ways to develop moral thinking in children through classroom discussion. 3.5 Multicultural diversity in the classroom : Meaning and concept of multiculturalism, Influence of language, religion, and culture on diversity among learners, Role of teacher in multicultural classroom. 3.6 Promoting Inclusion in the Classroom : Teaching strategies for students with diverse abilities and backgrounds, Ensuring equality and respect for all learners.

units.title: Contemporary Childhood and Emerging Issues Credit- 1
units.topics: 4.1 Understanding Contemporary Childhood: Meaning of “modern childhood”, Changing experiences of children in rural, urban, and tribal areas, Effects of poverty, migration, and social change. 4.2 Emerging Challenges in Childhood and Adolescence: Common issues: stress, anxiety, depression, behavioural problems; Peer pressure, bullying, and cyberbullying. Teacher’s role in supporting mental health. 4.3 Technology and Digital culture: Use and misuse of digital devices and the internet. Screen time, gaming, and social media. Role of educational technology (EdTech) in learning. 4.4 Political and Social Influences on Childhood: Types of government: democracy, socialism, and dictatorship, Influence of policies and political decisions on education and the growth of children. 4.5 Cultural Influences on Childhood: Importance of traditions, customs, and values. Role of cultural institutions and Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS) in development. 4.6 Media and Its Impact on Childhood: Types of media: print, electronic, and social; Positive and negative effects of media on children; Role of teachers in developing media awareness. units.title: Education in Contemporary Indian Society Credit- 1
units.topics: 1.1 Concept of Education – Meaning, definition, and aims of education in contemporary Indian society; foundation of sociology of education. 1.2 Nature of Indian Society – Diversity, unity, secularism, democracy, pluralism, and social structure. 1.3 Types of Education – Formal, Non-formal, Informal, Distance, and Open education. 1.4 Agencies of Education – Family, peer group, reference group, school, community, state, NGOs, and social media/online groups. 1.5 Role of Education in addressing Contemporary Issues – Education for social justice, environmental awareness, digital literacy, and human values. 1.6 Social Mobility in Indian Society – Nature, factors, and implications; education as a means of inclusive mobility.

units.title: Education and Social Change Credit- 1
units.topics: 2.1 Concept of Social Change – Meaning, definition, factors, and types of social change. 2.2 Social Changes in India – Transformation of social change through education. 2.3 Social Change and Indian Culture – Impact of social change on Indian culture. 2.4 Obstacles in Social Change – Casteism, poverty, gender discrimination, illiteracy, superstition, and resistance to innovation. 2.5 Role and Limitations of Education in Social Change – Role of education in promoting social transformation; integration of ethical and sustainable perspectives from Indian Knowledge Systems for balanced social development. 2.6 Benefits of Social Change to Family, Society, and Nation – Positive impact of social change on progress and development.

units.title: Gender and Education in India: Trends, Barriers and Transformative Practices
units.topics: Credit- 1 3.1 Concept of Gender – Meaning, definition, and difference between gender and sex. 3.2 Concept of Transgender – Meaning, definition, and place of transgender persons in society and educational institutions. 3.3 Education of Transgender – Present status, policies, and schemes for welfare and inclusion. 3.4 Gender and Schooling: Barriers to Gender Equality – Gender bias in textbooks, teacher behaviour, enrolment, dropout, classroom participation, social attitudes, early marriage, child labour, domestic responsibilities, and sexual abuse. 3.5 Role of Education in Promoting Gender Equality – Curriculum reforms, teacher training, inclusive practices, and pedagogical strategies for gender sensitization 3.6 Provisions for Gender Equality – Constitutional provisions (Articles 14, 15, 16), laws (POCSO, RTE), and policies for welfare.

units.topics: १.१ णहंदी णवषय का स्वरूप एवं महत्व ● णहंदी णवषय की प्रकृ णत और पररणि। ● णवद्यालयीन पाठ्यचयाय में णहंदी का स्र्थान। १.२ णहंदी णशक्षण के उिेश्य ● णवद्यालयीन स्तर पर णहंदी णशक्षण के उिेश्यों की व्याख्या। १.३ णहंदी णवषय का अनय णवषयों से संबंि एवं समस्याएँ ● णहंदी णवषय का अनय णवषयों से संबंि। ● णहंदी णवषय से संबंणित प्रमुख समस्याएँ। १.४ गद्य एवं पद्य णशक्षण की णवणियाँ ● गद्य (प्रोज़) णशक्षण की णवणियाँ। ● पद्य (काव्य) णशक्षण की णवणियाँ। १.५ व्याकरण एवं रचना णशक्षण की णवणियाँ ● व्याकरण णशक्षण की णवणियाँ। ● रचना (लेखन) णशक्षण की णवणियाँ। १.६ पठन एवं लेखन णशक्षण की णवणियाँ ● पठन (रीणडंग) णशक्षण की णवणियाँ। ● लेखन (राइणटंग) णशक्षण की णवणियाँ।

units.title: निंदी नवषय का नवश्ले षर् एवं नशिर्-संसाधन (क्र े नडट – १)
units.topics: २.१ णहंदी णवषय की संरचना ● णहंदी णवषय की रूपरेखा एवं संगठन। २.२ पाठ्यचयाय एवं पाठ्यक्रम ● णहंदी पाठ्यचयाय एवं पाठ्यक्रम की णवशेषताएँ। २.३ मूल्य एवं जीवन-कौशल ● णहंदी णवषय में णनणहत मूल्य एवं जीवन-कौशल। ● णहंदी पाठ्यपुस्तक का णवश्लेषण एवं णवषयवस्तु णवश्लेषण। २.४ णशक्षण-संसािनों की संकल्पना एवं महत्व ● णशक्षण-संसािनों की संकल्पना। ● आवश्यकता एवं महत्व। २.५ पारंपररक एवं प्रौद्योणगकी-आिाररत संसािन ● पुस्तकालय, श्यामपट, मुणद्रत सामग्री इत्याणद। ● ई-लणनिंग, णडणजटल टूल्स, ऐपस आणद। २.६ णहंदी प्रयोगशाला एवं णहंदी णशक्षक की भूणमका ● णहंदी प्रयोगशाला का महत्व। ● णहंदी णशक्षक के गुण एवं कक्षा में उनकी भूणमका। प्राययनिक कायय ( नीचे नदए िुए में से क े वल १) १. पाठ्यपुस्तक णवश्लेषण (समूह गणतणवणि के रूप में) – चुने हुए पाठ का शैणक्षक, भाषाई और मूल्यपरक णवश्लेषण कर प्रणतवेदन (ररपोटय) तैयार करना। २. शैणक्षक सहायक सािनों/पोस्टर का णनमायण और प्रस्तुतीकरण – स्वयं णनणमयत शैणक्षक सहायक सािन या पोस्टर तैयार कर कक्षा में प्रयोग कर प्रणतवेदन (ररपोटय) तैयार करना। ३. शैणक्षक क्षेत्र में अध्ययन भ्रमण एवं भाषा प्रयोगशाला का अवलोकन ररपोटय – णवद्यालय, भाषा प्रयोगशाला या णकसी शैणक्षक संस्र्थान में अध्ययन भ्रमण कर अवलोकन ररपोटय तैयार करना। ४. समूह चचाय एवं जीवन-कौशल समाकलन – णवद्याणर्थययों को समूहों में णवभाणजत ...

units.title: Foundations of The Indian Knowledge System (IKS) Credit 1
units.topics: 1.1 Indian Knowledge System (IKS): Concept, Definition, meaning, and philosophy of IKS; key features and foundations of Indian thought; comparison between Indian and Western views of knowledge. 1.2 Significance and Sources of IKS — Importance of IKS in contemporary education and nation-building; Primary and secondary sources such as the Vedas, Upanishads, oral traditions, folk knowledge, and community practices. 1.3 IKS and National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 — NEP provisions supporting IKS: value-based education, multilingualism, art integration, environmental awareness, and holistic learning. 1.4 Pañchakosha Framework — Concept of the five sheaths (Annamaya, Prānamaya, Manomaya, Vijñānamaya, Ānandamaya) from the Taittiriya Upanishad ; their educational and psychological significance. 1.5 Pañchakosha and Learner Development — Application of Pañchakosha for physical, emotional, intellectual, and spiritual growth of students. 1.6 Integrating Pañchakosha into Teaching–Learning — Classroom strategies and activities for implementing Pañchakosha-based holistic and inclusive education.

units.title: Key Domains of Indian Knowledge System (IKS) in School Education Credit 1
units.topics: 1.1 Philosophical and Spiritual Domain — Insights from Vedas, Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, Buddhist and Jain thought for developing self-knowledge, harmony, and ethical living. 1.2 Language, Literature, and Moral Domain — Teachings of Adi Shankaracharya, Kabir, Guru Nanak Dev Ji, Sant Dnyaneshwar, Sant Tukaram, and Swami Vivekananda; promoting values through literature and local languages. 1.3 Science and Mathematics Domain — Ancient Indian contributions to mathematics, astronomy, architecture, metallurgy, and environmental science; examples for integration in school subjects. 1.4 Health and Wellness Domain — Basic principles of Ayurveda, Yoga, and mindfulness for maintaining physical and mental well-being. 1.5 Culture and Arts Domain — Educational importance of Arthashastra, Natya Shastra, folk traditions, and storytelling; connecting students with cultural roots through arts and heritage. 1.6 Pedagogy and Values in Indian Tradition Traditional teaching methods like storytelling, questioning and experiential learning. Gurukul practices - Agama, Swadhyay, Pravachan, Vyavahar and and value- based learning; Ethics and discipline in Indian education.

units.title: Application of IKS in School Education Credit 1

units.title: Foundations of Digital Content Creation Credit- 1
units.topics: 1.1 Digital Learning and Content Creation: Meaning, concept, need, importance and characteristics of digital content in education. 1.2 Types of Digital Educational Content: Text, audio, video, images, animations, infographics and interactive digital resources. 1.3 Principles of Digital Content Design: Learner-centred design, instructional design, multimedia principles, accessibility and inclusivity. 1.4 Digital Content Development Process: Planning, designing, development, evaluation, sharing and revision of digital content. 1.5 NEP 2020 and NCFSE 2023 Perspectives: Digital education, technology integration, competency-based learning and digital literacy. 1.6 Digital Ethics and Responsible Use of Technology: Digital citizenship, cyber safety, copyright, Creative Commons, data privacy and ethical use of AI.

units.title: Digital Teaching-Learning Tools Credit- 1
units.topics: 2.1 Digital Teaching-Learning Tools: Concept, significance and selection of digital tools for classroom teaching. 2.2 Presentation and Multimedia Tools: Presentation tools, audio-video creation tools, screencasting and multimedia editing. 2.3 Interactive Learning and Assessment Tools: Digital quizzes, surveys, collaborative platforms and learner engagement tools. 2.4 Productivity and Collaboration Tools: Word processing, spreadsheets, cloud collaboration, digital whiteboards and classroom management tools. 2.5 Artificial Intelligence in Education: AI-assisted lesson planning, content generation, personalised learning and responsible use of AI. 2.6 Evaluation of Digital Resources: Quality standards, usability, accessibility, learner engagement and evaluation of digital content

units.title: Open Educational Resources Credit- 1
units.topics: 3.1 Foundations of Open Educational Resources: Meaning, evolution, principles, features and importance of OER. 3.2 Licensing and Copyright: Open licensing, Creative Commons licences, copyright, fair use and attribution. 3.3 OER in School Education: Benefits, challenges, curriculum integration and adaptation of OER. 3.4 National and State OER Platforms: DIKSHA, SWAYAM, e -Pathshala, e -Balbharati, YCMOU e-Books and other national repositories. 3.5 International OER Platforms: OER Commons, OpenStax, MERLOT and open -access educational repositories. 3.6 Selection and Evaluation of OER: Selection criteria, adaptation, localisation and evaluation of OER for classroom teaching.

units.title: Integration and Professional Practice Credit- 1
units.topics: 4.1 Integrating Digital Content and OER: Blended learning, flipped classroom, curriculum integration and learner engagement. 4.2 Digital Portfolio and Reflective Practice: E -portfolios, reflective journals, documentation and professional digital identity. 4.3 Teacher as Digital Content Creator: Content creation, peer review, resource sharing and continuous professional development. 4.4 Emerging Technologies in Education: Smart classrooms, mobile learning, augmented reality, virtual reality and learning analytics. 4.5 National and International Digital Education Initiatives: NETF, PM eVIDYA, Digital India, UNESCO OER Recommendation (2019) and global digital education initiatives. 4.6 Future Trends in Digital Education: Open education, artificial intelligence, adaptive learning and lifelong digital competencies Practical: (Any one from the given list) 1. subjects.title: Teacher Leadership and Professional Learning Communities

units.title: Foundations of Teacher Leadership and Professional Learning Communities
units.topics: Credit- 1 1.1 Teacher Leadership: Concept, meaning, nature, characteristics and significance of teacher leadership. 1.2 Professional Learning Communities (PLCs): Concept, principles, characteristics and importance of Professional Learning Communities. 1.3 Evolution and Relationship: Evolution, need and relationship between teacher leadership and Professional Learning Communities. 1.4 Teacher Leadership in Educational Policies: Teacher leadership in NEP 2020, NCFTE 2009, NCFSE 2023 and National Professional Standards for Teachers (NPST). 1.5 Professional Ethics and Reflective Practice: Professional ethics, accountability, reflective practice, lifelong learning and professional identity. 1.6 Teacher Leadership for School Improvement: Teacher as instructional leader, mentor, facilitator and change agent for improving school quality.

units.title: Teacher Leadership in Practice Credit- 1
units.topics: 2.1 Characteristics and Roles of Teacher Leaders: Leadership roles, responsibilities and professional competencies. 2.2 Leadership Styles in Education: Transformational, instructional, distributed and servant leadership. 2.3 Leadership Skills: Communication, collaboration, decision-making, problem-solving, mentoring and conflict resolution. 2.4 Instructional Leadership and Teacher Empowerment: Curriculum leadership, assessment, innovative pedagogy, teacher empowerment and learner achievement. 2.5 School Improvement and Action Research: School development planning, evidence- based practices and school-based action research. 2.6 Challenges and Opportunities: Challenges, opportunities and strategies for strengthening teacher leadership

units.title: Professional Learning Communities Credit- 1
units.topics: 3.1 Principles and Characteristics of PLCs: Concept, principles, characteristics and collaborative professional culture. 3.2 School-Based Professional Learning Communities: Collaborative lesson planning, lesson study, peer observation and reflective dialogue. 3.3 Professional Organisations and Teacher Networks: Teacher associations, subject associations, communities of practice and professional networks. 3.4 Digital Professional Learning Communities: Online communities, social media, webinars, MOOCs and digital learning platforms. 3.5 Professional Collaboration for School Improvement: Collaborative inquiry, mentoring, coaching, resource sharing and continuous professional learning. 3.6 Challenges and Opportunities of PLCs: Benefits, challenges and strategies for sustaining Professional Learning Communities.

units.title: Professional Development and Future-Ready Teacher Leadership Credit- 1
units.topics: 4.1 Continuous Professional Development (CPD): Concept, importance, lifelong learning and professional growth. 4.2 Professional Development Opportunities: In -service education, workshops, seminars, conferences, action research and certification programmes. 4.3 Digital Platforms for Professional Learning: DIKSHA, NISHTHA, SWAYAM, MOOCs, webinars and online professional learning platforms. 4.4 Professional Portfolio and Documentation: Professional portfolio, reflective journals, documentation of achievements and career progression. 4.5 Teacher Leadership, PLCs and School Development: Role of teacher leadership and PLCs in educational innovation, institutional development and quality improvement. 4.6 Future Trends in Teacher Leadership: Digital leadership, artificial intelligence, educational entrepreneurship, global competencies and future -ready teacher leadership.
